description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we are looking for candidates from the UK, Sweden, Spain or Germany.

About the role:

Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.

The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.

What You’ll Do

  • Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
  • Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
  • Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
  • Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
  • Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
  • Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
  • Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
  • Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
  • We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)

On-Call

Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
  • Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
  • Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
  • Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
  • Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
  • Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
  • Open-source contributions.
  • Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Databases SRE | Sweden | Remote
description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we are looking for candidates from the UK, Sweden, Spain or Germany.

About the role:

Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.

The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.

What You’ll Do

  • Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
  • Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
  • Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
  • Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
  • Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
  • Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
  • Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
  • Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
  • We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)

On-Call

Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
  • Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
  • Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
  • Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
  • Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
  • Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
  • Open-source contributions.
  • Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

title: Engineering Manager - Data Platform
description:
Within the Data Platform studio, we own two critical pillars: our event delivery platform that collects trillions of events per day from producers to consumers, and another, which handles the pseudonymisation of data so Spotify can use data responsibly and in compliance with privacy regulations. These systems sit at the heart of Spotify's data collection and are used by hundreds of teams across the company.

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of six experienced engineers distributed across Europe. You'll set the technical direction, ensure the team delivers high-impact work, and - just as importantly - invest deeply in the growth and careers of your engineers. If you're energised by both the technical challenges of large-scale data systems and the human side of building a high-performing team, we'd love to hear from you.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and develop a team of six experienced engineers, with a strong focus on coaching, career development, and creating an environment where people do the best work of their careers.
  • Take accountability for the team's delivery, ensuring clear priorities, healthy execution, and measurable outcomes.
  • Partner with product and stakeholders to shape the roadmap for event delivery and privacy infrastructure.
  • Drive technical strategy and architectural decisions for systems operating at Spotify scale.
  • Build a culture of ownership, psychological safety, and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate across Data Platform and the wider engineering organisation to align on shared goals and dependencies.
  • Manage on-call health, operational excellence, and reliability for the team's services.
  • Actively participate in hiring, onboarding, and growing the team's capabilities.

Who You Are

  • You have experience managing teams of senior/experienced engineers and understand that people leadership is your primary craft, not a side responsibility.
  • You have a track record of investing in engineers' careers - running meaningful development conversations, helping people grow into new roles, and creating clarity around expectations and progression.
  • You're comfortable with distributed data systems, event-driven architectures, or data infrastructure at scale - you don't need to write the code, but you can engage credibly in technical discussions and unblock your team.
  • You hold yourself and your team accountable for outcomes, not just activity.
  • You communicate clearly and build trust across functions and time zones.
  • You've worked with distributed teams and understand how to create cohesion and inclusion when people aren't in the same room.
  • You're excited about the potential of AI and LLMs to transform how engineering teams work - whether that's accelerating development workflows, rethinking how data infrastructure is built and operated, or helping your team adopt AI-assisted tooling effectively.

Where You’ll Be

  • This role is based in London.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! title: Account Partner - Veeva Basics (Existing Customers)
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
 
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
 
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
 
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

We are looking for a tenured Account Partner to manage our existing European customers across Veeva Basics, a suite of highly scalable out of the box R&D applications that support emerging biotechs by saving them time, money and valuable resources. This product has already transformed the industry and remains the only platform of its kind on the market. 

As an Account Partner for Veeva Basics you will be responsible for meeting annual sales goals and helping the team achieve our long-range growth targets. In this role, you will champion customer success by driving product adoption through maximising the value our existing customers receive, ensuring account retention, maximizing the value our existing customers receive and identifying new growth opportunities in these accounts. You will hold established executive relationships and ensure our vision is evangelized.

What You'll Do

  • Be the go to person for our customers in Europe
  • Evangelize the “why” and value with a focus on our vision of becoming recognized as the industry standard for emerging biotechs
  • Retain our accounts, drive on time renewals and upsell new applications
  • Understand and execute the sales cycles, utilizing internal and external resources as appropriate
  • Create, run and execute regional communities of practice at an executive level
  • Understand Veeva Basics products and work with internal colleagues to build a sales strategy
  • Keep current with industry trends and engage customers in addressing their business challenges
  • Act with urgency, integrity, and a relentless focus on customer success
  • Meet/Exceed pipeline generation and cross selling revenue targets

Requirements

  • 5+ years of work experience.
  • Including 3+ years from R&D domains
  • SaaS or similar services selling into Life Sciences
  • Experience selling complementary or competitive solutions into R&D
  • Have entrepreneurial instincts. Ability to define a strategy for your region and execute on it
  • Must be highly self-motivated and be drawn to the reality of a start up business.
  • Passion and demonstrated results in a sales role to C-Level executives.
  • Ability to articulate business cases and value propositions to C-Level executives.
  • Curate executive level communities and round tables with the support of marketing
  • Have a creative mindset to think outside the box and make ideas reality

Nice to Have

  • Experience of building and owning community forums and events

Interviewing with Veeva

    We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.
  • Follow the application process and submit your resume.
  • Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.
  • Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email with our decision.
  • If moving to the interview stage, the process is as follows:
    1. A conversation with the hiring manager
    2. A practical case exercise
    3. A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader.
  • Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Woodlands Primary School

Woodlands Primary School is a warm, nurturing and ambitious primary school serving the Gleadless and Norton community in south Sheffield.

The school is driven by a simple but powerful belief that education changes lives, with high expectations for every child and a commitment to ensuring all pupils can achieve their full potential.

  • developing and implementing a curriculum that is aligned with the early years foundation stage framework and school policies

  • working collaboratively with colleagues to ensure consistency of practice and high standards across the school
  • supporting and encouraging student well-being, ensuring that all students are able to achieve their full potential.

Candidates must have the ability to engage, inspire and motivate both pupils and colleagues and have the strategic vision to be part of the team moving our vibrant school forward.

They will also have the ability to forge excellent relationships with colleagues, parents and most importantly, our children. They must be team players who are exceptional teachers of English and mathematics, as well as having the knowledge and skills to inspire children’s learning in all wider areas of the curriculum.

If you are a dedicated and passionate teacher with a desire to make a real difference in the lives of children, then we want to hear from you.

title: Site Technician - Apprentice
description:
Haydon is a large, friendly and creative school in North West London, judged Good by Ofsted. We are seeking a proactive, organised and committed Site Technician - Apprentice to join our friendly and dedicated Site Team. This is an important role in supporting the school to maintain a safe, compliant and positive environment for our students, staff and visitors. Working collaboratively across the school, you will play a key role in promoting a strong culture of health and safety, ensuring statutory requirements are met and contributing to the continuous improvement of our premises, systems and working practices. We are looking for someone who is passionate about creating safe, inclusive and well-managed environments and who can bring a practical, solution-focused approach to the role.

The Role:

Security and Safeguarding

  • To take all reasonable steps to minimise loss or damage to the property of the school, its employees or the other users of the site and protect the overall security of the site. As a key holder, responding in person to emergency call outs at any time as required.

  • To open up and check the school site in the mornings. To secure the school premises at the end of the day; checking the premises to ensure that all occupants have vacated the site, all windows and doors are closed and locked, all electrical equipment is switched off, activating intruder alarms and ensuring the safekeeping of keys to the premises.

  • To monitor CCTV where appropriate, acting proactively to follow up on any issues of security, safeguarding or behaviour of students or visitors identified on the footage.

  • To ensure the safeguarding of students by:

    • ensuring that the school’s boundary is maintained securely

    • ensuring that any areas of the school without supervision are kept secure throughout the school day

    • providing appropriate CCTV footage to senior staff as required to address any issues

    Maintenance and Cleaning

    • To carry out maintenance work including repairs on buildings, including all the fixtures, fittings and grounds across the school site, delivering an excellent environment for teaching and learning for our students and staff.

    • To proactively check and address the cleanliness and tidiness of the whole site multiple times each day, with litter picking and sweeping of the site being carried out to the same frequency and to a high standard, with particular attention being paid to the cleanliness of the toilets.

    • To check the condition of the buildings on a regular basis as directed and take appropriate action in the event of essential maintenance or repairs being required.

    • To use appropriate systems (such as an electronic system for site requests to be made by school staff directly to the Site Team) to ensure that all work is acted upon in accordance with standard operating procedures.

    • To respond to routine emergencies at any time and undertake appropriate repairs, giving priorities to matters affecting health and safety and safeguarding.

    • To carry out decoration and improvement work as directed.

    • To undertake cleaning and maintenance duties as required including sweeping the grounds, emptying bins and recycling, removing graffiti, chewing gum, litter and weeds, cleaning windows, spills and bodily fluids, cleaning of staffroom and toilets etc.

    Health and Safety Regulations

    • To follow health and safety regulations throughout the site.

    • To stay up to date on all relevant health and safety policy and regulations, attending training courses as appropriate.

    • To carry out all appropriate security and health and safety checks (in accordance with local policy, HASAW, CLEAPS, COSSH, asbestos, water hygiene, PAT testing and other regulations) in all areas of the buildings, grounds and equipment, as directed.

    • To be familiar with the fire evacuation procedure and take the necessary steps during a fire evacuation.

    • To be up to date on all required training such as manual handling, ladder use, etc.

    Porterage

    • To provide a responsive, flexible porterage service for the movement of equipment and furniture around the site according to need.

    • To set up and clear venues to brief and to a high standard in advance of assemblies, meetings, performances, events, exams, lettings and other activities.

    • To ensure that classrooms are ready for lessons on time whenever they have had their layout changed for any purpose.

    • To ensure that the school site is clean, clear and in a suitable condition for use by lettings at the end of the school day.

    • To ensure the timely delivery of all parcels to their recipient, ensuring that appropriate procedures are followed.

    General Responsibilities

    • To contribute to the overall ethos/work/aims of the school.

    • To take the lead on one or more areas of the site team’s responsibilities, as directed, and become the main point of contact or expert on that area, identifying and undertaking any required CPD as a result.

    • To communicate effectively with professionalism and respect, forming excellent working relationships with students, staff, Governors, visitors and contractors.

    • To understand and actively promote all school policies and procedures.

    • To commit to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.

    • To be a fire marshal, undertake the necessary training and carry out fire marshal duties as required.

    • To be a first aider, undertake the necessary training and carry out first aid duties as required.

    • To take responsibility for your own professional development by actively seeking formal and informal learning opportunities and by actively engaging in the school CPD programme and appraisal process.

    • To recognise own strengths and areas of expertise and use these to support and develop others.

    • To take responsibility for your own physical and emotional health, so that you attend school regularly.

    • To attend and participate in meetings as required.

    • To treat all users of the school with courtesy and consideration.

    • To be aware of the school’s place in the local community and work closely with neighbours to ensure a positive impact on the local area.

    • To present a positive personal image, complying with the dress code and contributing to a welcoming environment which supports equal opportunities for all.

    • To promote and ensure the health and safety of students, staff and visitors at all times.

    Note: All Haydon employees are expected to be flexible in undertaking the duties and responsibilities attached to their post and may be asked to perform other duties.

    WORK ENVIRONMENT

    The post holder will be based within the Site Office, but will be required to work throughout the site, including outside, in the “void” spaces under the school, boiler rooms, cleaning cupboards, the roofs, and other locations, taking appropriate safety steps.

    The post will involve physical activity including cleaning, maintenance, lifting and manual handling.

    This is an all year round post. The post holder is required to work 37 hours per week between 7.00am and 11pm Monday to Sunday (shift work Monday to Sunday - two days of the shift will always be on Saturday and Sunday, remaining three days will vary in line with work requirements), with an hour for lunch, to be taken according to the lunchtime rota. The post holder is required to work on all INSET days. The post holder should expect to take the majority of their annual leave outside of school holidays as these are particularly busy periods for maintenance, building, cleaning and decoration works.

Haydon is a large, welcoming and diverse secondary school in North West London, proudly judged Good by Ofsted. title: Food Technician
description:
Job description

Job title:

Food Technician

Grade:

Salary dependent on qualifications and experience

Hours / weeks:

37 hours per week(8am -4pm),Term Time plus 5 INSET days

Contract type:

Permanent

Reports to:

Head of Food Department

Job purpose

  • The Food Technician provides high-quality technical, organisational and practical support for the Food Preparation and Nutrition department. The postholder should ensure that ingredients, equipment and teaching spaces are ready for effective learning; supports safe practical work; and helps maintain a calm, hygienic and well-organised environment in which students can develop confidence, independence and practical food skills.

  • To contribute to the overall ethos, work and aims of the Academy.

Main responsibilities A. Preparation for teaching and practical lessons
  • Prepare, weigh, portion, label and organise food ingredients required for practical lessons, demonstrations, assessments, clubs and other departmental activities.

  • Set out suitable equipment, utensils, appliances and resources in advance of lessons, following teachers' instructions and schemes of work.

  • Prepare demonstration areas and, where requested, assist with the preparation of exemplar dishes, samples or visual resources.

  • Check lesson requirements in advance and inform teaching staff promptly of shortages, substitutions, equipment faults or other concerns.

  • Support the orderly collection, distribution and return of ingredients and equipment before, during and after practical sessions.

  • Assist with the organisation of ingredients and equipment for GCSE practical assessments and controlled assessment-related activities, in line with relevant examination requirements and staff direction.



B. Support during practical sessions

  • Provide practical support to teaching staff and students during Food Preparation and Nutrition lessons, while working under the direction of the class teacher.

  • Reinforce safe and hygienic working routines, including correct use of equipment, cleaning procedures and prevention of cross-contamination.

  • Offer appropriate practical guidance that helps students develop skills, independence and confidence without replacing the teacher's role or completing assessed work for them.

  • Support individual students and small groups when directed, including students with additional needs, by clarifying routines, helping them organise their workspace and encouraging safe participation.

  • Respond calmly and promptly to minor spills, breakages and practical issues, and immediately report accidents, hazards, unsafe behaviour or safeguarding concerns to the appropriate member of staff.

C. Hygiene, cleaning, health and safety

  • Maintain consistently high standards of cleanliness and hygiene in food rooms, preparation areas, storage spaces, refrigerators, freezers, sinks, work surfaces and shared equipment.

  • Ensure aprons, tea towels and dish cloths are washed and ready for use daily.

  • Complete routine cleaning and disinfection tasks before and after practical work, following food-safe cleaning schedules and relevant risk assessments.

  • Monitor refrigerator and freezer temperatures, food storage, date labels, allergen information and stock rotation, keeping accurate records where required.

  • Follow safe procedures for food handling, storage and disposal, including separation of raw and ready-to-eat foods and management of allergen risks.

  • Check that equipment is safe and suitable for use; remove defective items from service, label them clearly and report faults promptly.

  • Ensure emergency and safety equipment is accessible and report any concerns relating to first-aid supplies, fire safety, electrical safety or gas appliances through the Academy's procedures.

  • Contribute to departmental risk assessments, COSHH records, hygiene checks and other health and safety documentation as directed.

D. Equipment, stock and resources

  • Maintain an accurate and orderly inventory of ingredients, consumables, utensils, small equipment and other departmental resources.

  • Check stock levels regularly; identify future needs; prepare orders for authorisation; and liaise with approved suppliers in accordance with Academy purchasing procedures.

  • Receive and check deliveries for quantity, quality, damage, use-by dates, temperature and accuracy, reporting discrepancies promptly.

  • Rotate stock using first-in, first-out principles and dispose of unsuitable food and waste safely, responsibly and in line with Academy procedures.

  • Clean, inspect and carry out permitted routine care of equipment, arranging repair or servicing through the designated member of staff when required.

  • Organise cupboards, stores and preparation areas so that resources are clearly labelled, secure, accessible and easy to audit.

  • Support cost control by monitoring waste, portioning accurately, seeking value for money and maintaining appropriate records of expenditure or lesson costs.


E. Departmental and wider Academy support

  • Work closely with the Curriculum Leader and teaching staff to plan technical support and anticipate departmental needs.

  • Assist with displays, open evenings, enrichment activities, food clubs, educational visits, special events and transition activities where reasonably required.

  • Contribute to the development of efficient departmental systems, cleaning schedules, stock records and safe operating procedures.

  • Participate in relevant training, meetings, performance development and whole-Academy activities appropriate to the role.

  • Maintain confidentiality and handle information in accordance with data-protection requirements and Academy policies.

  • Undertake other duties consistent with the nature and level of the post, as reasonably directed by the line manager or Headteacher.
    This is not an exhaustive list of duties; they may be varied from time to time without changing the general character of the job or the level of responsibility. A high degree of flexibility and adaptability is an important element of this role.

The duties and responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present. This role will be reviewed annually as part of the performance appraisal process and the post holder is expected to accept any reasonable alterations that may from time to time be necessary.

Westfield Academy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of Children and Young people. To meet this responsibility, we follow a rigorous selection process. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check.



Person specification

Attributes

Essential (or expected to train / qualify to that standard)


Desirable

Qualifications and training

  • Good standard of general education, including literacy and numeracy.

  • Food hygiene qualification at Level 2 or willingness to obtain it promptly.

  • Willingness to complete relevant health and safety, safeguarding, allergen and first-aid training.

  • Level 2 or 3 food hygiene, food safety, catering or related qualification.

  • Relevant technician, catering or education-support training.

Knowledge

  • Sound knowledge of food hygiene, safe food storage, cleaning and prevention of cross-contamination.

  • Awareness of food allergens and the importance of accurate ingredient information.

  • Understanding of safe use of common kitchen tools and appliances.

  • Knowledge of school Food Preparation and Nutrition practical work, GCSE practical assessment requirements, food allergen awareness, COSHH or departmental risk assessment.

Experience

  • Practical experience of food preparation, catering, hospitality, food education or a comparable setting.

  • Experience of maintaining clean, organised work areas and managing supplies.

  • Previous experience as a school technician or in a role supporting young people.

  • Experience of ordering, inventory control, budgeting or equipment maintenance.

Skills and abilities

  • Strong organisation and time-management skills.

  • Ability to follow instructions, plan ahead and work independently.

  • Clear communication and positive interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to maintain accurate records and use basic digital systems.

  • Ability to work safely and calmly in a busy practical environment.

  • Ability to adapt recipes, quantities or resources to meet lesson needs.

  • Confidence supporting demonstrations, enrichment activities or practical events.

Personal qualities

  • Reliable, punctual, flexible and proactive.

  • Patient and encouraging when working with students.

  • High standards of cleanliness and attention to detail.

  • Commitment to teamwork, equality, inclusion and professional conduct.

  • Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.

  • Enthusiasm for food education, nutrition and helping young people develop life skills.

The ElevenLabs Impact Program exists to democratize access to our technology and make AI work for all people, supporting for-good use cases across healthcare, education, and culture. We're looking for a Producer to own the external storytelling and event presence for Impact, a role that coordinates PR, agency management, social launches, documentary-style case studies, and event production. This is a hands-on, in-house role: you're the person who makes sure every launch, film, and activation meets (or, ideally raises) the bar of the rest of the company's output, working closely with our internal Design, Comms, and Events teams, and, when applicable, with the external agencies and production teams supporting PR, film, and creative execution.   • Manage multiple concurrent launches, shoots, and events at once.

  • A great project manager with a sharp creative eye, someone who runs cross-functional logistics flawlessly, has real taste, and will push the team to hit it.

  • Proven practical experience working with vulnerable communities, especially people living with a disability, and ensuring they are provided the time, space and accommodation to be equal partners in high-pressure productions, on tight timelines, and in public.

title: Strategic Account Executive, EMEA (100% hunting role)
description:
Sonatype is the software supply chain security company. Sonatype is accelerating the future of agentic software development. As developers and AI agents build faster than ever, enterprises need a new level of control, visibility, and confidence at the moment software is assembled. Our Nexus One platform helps development, security, and platform teams govern the components, dependencies, models, and artifacts that power modern applications without slowing innovation down.

We are uniquely positioned to lead this next era. Sonatype operates both Maven Central, one of the world’s largest public open source registries, and Nexus Repository, a top-ranked enterprise repository used by thousands of organizations and over 70% of the Fortune 100. With over 1 trillion downloads annually across our ecosystem, we have unmatched visibility into how software is published, consumed, and propagated. That insight helps our customers make smarter decisions earlier, reduce rework, avoid security surprises, and ship AI-powered software with greater speed and confidence.

We are seeking an exceptional Enterprise Account Executive to accelerate Sonatype's growth across one of the most commercially significant and competitive enterprise technology markets.

This is a pure new-logo acquisition role for an accomplished enterprise hunter who thrives on creating opportunities, displacing established competitors and winning complex, high-value enterprise business.

As artificial intelligence transforms how software is developed, organisations are facing unprecedented challenges around open source security, software supply chain integrity, developer productivity and governance.

Sonatype operates at the intersection of these challenges, helping some of the world's largest organisations build and deploy software securely through industry-leading software supply chain intelligence and an integrated platform spanning repository management, application security and malware prevention.

The territory presents an opportunity for a commercially ambitious seller to develop strategic enterprise relationships, challenge established technology providers and build a significant new-business pipeline.

You will own a defined portfolio of enterprise prospects, with a clear mandate to identify, develop and close new-logo opportunities.

This is not an account management position, nor is it a role designed around managing an inherited customer portfolio.

Your success will be defined by the new customers you acquire, the competitive opportunities you create and the revenue you generate.

You will be expected to operate confidently against an annual quota, bringing the commercial discipline, enterprise sales experience and competitive intensity required to deliver sustained performance.

We're particularly interested in speaking with consistently high-performing enterprise sellers who have achieved President's Club, Pinnacle Club or equivalent recognition and can demonstrate repeated success in complex, competitive technology markets.

Our role in detail:

Territory Development & Strategic New-Logo Acquisition:

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive enterprise territory strategy across prospect accounts.

  • Take full accountability for new-logo acquisition, building and converting a sustainable pipeline of high-value enterprise opportunities.

  • Identify and prioritise strategic prospects based on enterprise size, software development complexity, security maturity, competitive landscape and commercial potential.

  • Build sophisticated account plans identifying organisational structures, executive stakeholders, buying committees, incumbent technology providers and potential entry points.

  • Generate significant self-sourced pipeline through proactive outbound prospecting, executive engagement, targeted account-based campaigns and strategic networking.

  • Establish relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, VP Engineering, DevSecOps, Platform Engineering and Application Security leadership.

  • Engage enterprise prospects before formal buying processes begin, helping customers recognise challenges and opportunities they may not yet be actively addressing.

  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Engineering, Channel and executive leadership to develop coordinated account acquisition strategies.

  • Identify opportunities to position Sonatype's broader software supply chain platform through compelling customer-specific business cases.

  • Maintain strong commercial discipline around pipeline coverage, opportunity qualification, deal progression and forecasting.

    • Competitive Displacement & Enterprise Deal Execution:

    Competitive displacement will be a significant component of this role.

    We are looking for someone who understands the enterprise cybersecurity, DevSecOps and developer tooling landscape and is confident challenging established technology providers.

    You will be expected to:

    • Identify enterprise accounts using competing or incumbent software supply chain, repository management and application security technologies.

    • Develop account-specific competitive displacement strategies based on customer challenges, technical requirements and business outcomes.

    • Demonstrate a strong understanding of the competitive landscape, including organisations such as JFrog, Snyk, Black Duck, Mend, GitHub, GitLab, Checkmarx and Veracode.

    • Understand where Sonatype's intelligence, security capabilities, platform breadth and preventative approach provide meaningful customer differentiation.

    • Lead sophisticated enterprise sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, technical evaluations, proofs of value, procurement and executive decision-making.

    • Develop strong economic buyer relationships and build compelling financial, operational and security business cases.

    • Apply structured enterprise sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC to establish clear qualification, decision criteria, competitive positioning and mutual action plans.

    • Navigate complex negotiations and commercial discussions while maintaining strong customer relationships.

    • Build internal and external champions capable of influencing enterprise purchasing decisions.

    • Demonstrate the judgement to qualify out opportunities where genuine customer value or a viable purchasing path cannot be established.

      • We want a seller who knows how to win when the customer already has a solution, not someone who only succeeds when there is no competition.

      Industry Knowledge & Technical Credibility:

      This role requires a strong understanding of the market in which Sonatype operates.

      You should be comfortable discussing how modern enterprise organisations develop, secure and deploy software, and how AI is changing the speed and complexity of those processes.

      You will:

      • Understand the commercial and technical challenges associated with open source software, software composition analysis, DevSecOps and application security.

      • Engage confidently with technical and executive buyers around software supply chain risk, developer productivity, governance and security.

      • Position Sonatype's platform capabilities across Nexus Repository, Firewall, Lifecycle and related solutions.

      • Understand how software supply chain intelligence can help organisations identify vulnerable components, prevent malicious packages entering development and make better risk decisions.

      • Translate technical capabilities into measurable business outcomes rather than relying on feature-led selling.

      • Recognise opportunities to position Sonatype as a strategic enterprise platform rather than a standalone point solution.

      • Stay informed about emerging technology, AI-assisted development, competitive market movements and evolving enterprise security requirements.

        Enterprise sales success requires the ability to bring the right expertise together around the customer.

        You will:

        • Build productive relationships with regional channel partners, systems integrators and enterprise solution providers.

        • Identify partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities that support new-logo acquisition.

 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

 About the role:

 The Account Development Representative (ADR) job is the launching point for an individual looking for a successful career in SaaS sales. In this role, you will be at the front of Samsara’s go-to-market strategy. This includes hunting for leads, mapping enterprise accounts, and building demand for Samsara’s full line of products. This role is ideal for individuals looking to develop enterprise technology sales skills and to advance their careers. Successful ADRs earn accelerated commissions and head down the path for promotion into closing roles. You will work closely with top-tier executives and will see up close how sales organizations succeed.

 This is a hybrid position open to candidates residing in Phoenix Metro Area of Arizona, requiring 3 days per week onsite and 2 days remote.

 You should apply if :

• You want to impact the industries that run our world : Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• You are the architect of your own career : If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. Successful ADRs can see promotion to a closing role in two years or less.

• You love talking to people : In this role you will average 50 calls to prospective customers daily.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work : One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You treat rejection as a learning experience : In this role, you will get hung up on and you will get told no. You need to have resilience to pick up the phone again and again to sell Samsara’s mission.

• You want to be with the best : Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

 Minimum requirements for this role :

• Ability and willingness to make 50 cold calls a day.

• At least 6 months of sales experience and/or sales prospecting ability. This can be sales related coursework, sales competitions, etc.

• Must be currently enrolled in an accredited 4-year Bachelor's degree program or within 1 year of graduation

 An ideal candidate has :

• Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process

• 6 Months experience with Salesforce, LI Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo.

• Ability to quickly grasp technical concepts and embed AI usage into day to day operations

title: Staff Software Engineer - Databases SRE | Spain | Remote
description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity and we are looking for candidates from the UK, Sweden, Spain or Germany.

About the role:

Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.

The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.

What You’ll Do

  • Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
  • Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
  • Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
  • Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
  • Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
  • Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
  • Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
  • Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
  • We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)

On-Call

Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
  • Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
  • Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
  • Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
  • Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
  • Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
  • Open-source contributions.
  • Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

title: Site Selection & Colocation Manager – Data Centers
description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

The Site Selection & Colocation Manager is responsible for identifying, evaluating, and securing optimal locations for new data center developments and colocation expansions. This role combines real estate strategy, technical due diligence, market analysis, and vendor management to support the company’s global data center growth. The manager will collaborate closely with engineering, construction, finance, legal, and network planning teams to ensure that selected sites meet operational, technical, and business requirements.

You’re welcome to work in our office in Amsterdam or Remote in the EU.

Your responsibilities will include:

Site Selection & Market Analysis

  • Lead the end-to-end site selection process for new data center facilities.
  • Conduct market assessments, including power availability, fiber connectivity, land suitability, regulatory requirements, and risk factors.
  • Build and maintain market intelligence on emerging data center regions, supply trends, energy markets, and colocation pricing.
  • Evaluate and shortlist candidate sites through comparative analysis, scoring models, and feasibility studies.

Technical & Environmental Due Diligence

  • Coordinate environmental, geotechnical, hydrological, and seismic assessments.
  • Assess infrastructure availability (power, water, fiber) and future scalability.
  • Evaluate construction constraints, climate conditions, logistics access, and permitting feasibility.
  • Work with engineering teams to ensure sites meet mechanical, electrical, and network resilience requirements.

Colocation Strategy & Vendor Management

  • Identify colocation providers and evaluate facilities based on technical specifications, SLA requirements, and cost structure.
  • Lead RFPs, negotiations, and contract execution with colocation and connectivity partners.
  • Manage colocation lifecycle: renewals, expansions, migrations, and optimization of space/power allocations.
  • Monitor vendor performance against SLA, uptime, compliance, and efficiency metrics.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work with data center design and construction teams to validate site feasibility and development timelines.
  • Partner with legal on contract terms, property acquisition, lease terms, and regulatory compliance.
  • Support finance with CapEx/OpEx modeling, ROI calculations, and business case development.
  • Coordinate with public authorities, utilities, and permitting agencies as needed.

Risk Assessment & Compliance

  • Evaluate risks related to natural hazards, geopolitical risk, security, environmental constraints, and utility reliability.
  • Ensure compliance with local regulations, zoning laws, and corporate standards.
  • Maintain documentation for audits, reporting, and internal approvals.

We expect you to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Real Estate, Engineering, Business, Geography, or related field.
  • 5–8+ years of experience in site selection, real estate development, colocation management, or data center infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of data center power, cooling, and network requirements.
  • Experience in evaluating colocation providers and negotiating leases/SLAs.
  • Analytical skills in market research, cost modeling, and risk assessment.
  • Ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects across regions.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with hyperscale or large-scale data center development.
  • Knowledge of utility procurement (power, water), renewable energy markets, and substation planning.
  • Familiarity with geospatial tools (GIS), risk modeling, or data center capacity planning.
  • Understanding of permitting processes and environmental regulations.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.

The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.

What You’ll Do

  • Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
  • Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
  • Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
  • Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
  • Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
  • Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
  • Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
  • Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
  • We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)

On-Call

Weekday on-call is 12-hour shifts, Monday to Friday, split between North America and Europe so you cover your local working hours. Weekends are covered by a separate 24-hour rotation. You’ll take a weekend roughly once every six to eight weeks.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
  • Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
  • Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
  • Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
  • Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
  • Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.

Nice to Have:

    • Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
    • Open-source contributions.
    • Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

In Germany, the Base compensation range for this role is €109,709 - €131,651. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable) and other benefits listed here.#LI-Remote

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.

title: Senior Solutions Engineer
description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
.

See yourself at Twilio

Join us as our next Senior Solutions Engineer on Twilio’s Digital Sales Communications team!

About the job

This position is needed to enable our customers to build the future of communications. The Senior Solutions Engineer is a critical part of the sales team focused on our Digital Sales segment.

Twilio’s Senior Solutions Engineers are responsible for delivering the technical win and best product fit to our customers.They lead the technical pre-sales relationship, drive technical discovery, propose technical architectures, demonstrate the product, anticipate concerns and offer creative solutions. They build customer trust in Twilio’s solutions.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Partner with Account Executives to execute pre-sales activities including opportunity qualification, demonstrations, Proof-of-Concept, RFP, design documentation, technical presentations and enablement sessions.
  • Help customers achieve success by leading the technical and product sale, recommending best-practice solutions, and guiding them on how to use Twilio’s APIs.
  • Establish yourself as a trusted advisor to our customers, by taking the lead on understanding customer technical pains through discovery in order to design, demonstrate, and present innovative solutions that solve business challenges.
  • Build and present highly interactive, complex and engaging customer product demonstrations to help showcase the capabilities of Twilio’s Communications Products, while effectively forming strong customer relationships with both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Be Hands-on, high-energy, passionate, and a creative problem solver, equipped with the knowledge of how to get things done and ability to lead others to success.
  • Take the initiative to identify and solve problems - both for the customer and within the organization as we grow.
  • Contribute to the broader Twilio Solutions Engineering community through knowledge sharing, constructing demonstration materials, and creating reusable presentations.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • 5+ years of pre-sales experience selling complex, technical products or 3+ years of professional experience supporting technical products coupled with customer facing experience, particularly in delivery or consulting.
  • Excellent communicator and presenter able to gain audience confidence.
  • An engaging storyteller - you can gain audience confidence and communicate complex topics to multiple levels of audience.
  • Ability to build a deep understanding of a customer’s communications needs and guide them to a technical solution.
  • Previous software development experience or working knowledge in one or more of the following areas:
    • Backend (Java, C#, Node.js, Python, PHP)
    • Web development (JavaScript, HTML/CSS, frontend frameworks - React, Vue.js, Angular)
    • Experience building with REST APIs
  • Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in a technical discipline (Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science) or equivalent practical experience.

Desired:

  • Familiarity with cloud platforms (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure) and cloud application architecture.
  • Previous experience in Telecom, SIP, Contact Center, or Security is a plus.
  • Experience with sales methodologies.

Location

This role will be remote AND based in the United Kingdom.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 10% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

.

Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.
